findings.text: _answer_instant duplicates reckon/_timestamps.py:parse_utc: the same strip, fromisoformat, malformed-returns-None rule, and the same naive-read-as-UTC policy, which parse_utc's module docstring states as the repository's one parser that callers are meant to migrate to; plan_review already imports it elsewhere. _commit_time at :1574 repeats the same parse on git's %cI output as well, so the module now carries two more hand-rolled copies of a rule it already imports.

The delta's whole performance repair lives in the line-anchor branch of _acted_finding_units (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2300-2322): the anchor is classified without text, line anchors are collected and resolved lazily through the new reviewed_text callable, and units already covered are dropped. This file's only finding anchor is the section form '#s5', and no test in the tree stores an acted finding with a plan-line anchor, so a regression that resolved no line anchor, or that read the wrong revision's text, would leave the gate green; the case the repair exists for has no assertion under it.

reviewed_text_of keys its memo on (plan_path, reviewed_blob_sha) and not on the review it belongs to, so every record for a plan that carries no reviewed_blob_sha collapses onto one key and a later review's line anchor is resolved against the first such record's snapshot; two reviews of one plan taken before and after an edit would then map a line to different sections than their own snapshots would give. Records written by the current store always carry the blob, so this is a narrowing of the fallback rather than a live defect, but the key does not identify the text it caches.
